questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- It was crucial that it was an English speaking country
- It was crucial that it had the mandatory class that i had to get
- It was crucial that it was far away from home

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I met some absolutely amazing people and i learned a lot about my self, but I think the university could have done more for the exchange students which would have made it a better exchange stay.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yes, this was very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really need any assistance upon arrival

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my network but it was still quite difficult so i would really recommend starting the search for somewhere to live quite early.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should know that it makes social things a bit more difficult, and that the public transportation system isn't that reliable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is extremely expensive, and they mostly rent out for 6 months period but as an exchange student you aren't really there for more than 4 months.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is good ressources that makes you able to organize your courses so they fit into a schedule, and the registration process is quite simple.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Going to the website and signing up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You were able to contact the university with questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advice them to do it as early as possible to make sure you get the courses you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did 1 first year class, 1 second year class and 2 third year classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is quite different, you have the same type of lectures but it is mostly the tutorials that are different. They only last 1 hour and in most of the classes this is not the time to ask questions, often they go through an assignment you have handed in or they might be presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to comparative politics 
Intermediate macroeconomics II
Resource and environmental economics III
Money, banking and financial markets III

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend intermediate macroeconomics, and if you are up for a challenge then also Money, banking and financial markets.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't really think there were any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Getting the visa is quite expensive compared to what I expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a lot of clubs which is really great social opportunities for exchange students. They have all types of sports and they have student organizations and way more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was a part of the rowing club which was a really great experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Kayaking with dolphins i Port Adelaide and there is other opportunities to swim with dolphins as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite okay, there is definitely some small talk that you have to get used to, and that cars is the main form of transportation.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Joining the clubs at uni.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and friendliness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be really socially active in the beginning, be open to new opportunities and if you want to do something with other exchange students just ask because most of them wants to do as much as possible and get to know as many people as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't have a lot of plans before you arrive, and then plan it with all the other people.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing wanting to explore Australia while still wanting to do well at uni.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
